sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of an employee's own requests and manager team views; status: filtering pending approvals and status-based queries; start_date: range queries for calendar/team views and overlap checks; leave_type_id: filtering by leave type

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: balance lookups for an employee; policy_id: entitlement lookups per policy; fiscal_year: year-scoped balance queries; employee_id + policy_id + fiscal_year: unique balance row lookup during approval/deduction

table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: manager_id: team views for manager approval workflows; email: unique lookup for auth/identity; employee_number: unique business identifier lookup

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: resolving the governing policy for a leave type; is_active: filtering active policies during entitlement resolution

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type + entity_id: audit history for a specific entity; performed_at: time-ordered audit reports

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: inbox lookups for a user; status: filtering unread/pending notifications
data_notes: Six conceptual tables: leave_requests, leave_balances, employees, leave_policies, audit_logs, notifications. All repositories backed by PostgreSQL via the shared pg Pool (src/shared/db/connection.ts). Audit (GP-002) and RBAC (GP-005) are enforced at the service/controller layer; the audit_logs table persists every state-changing operation. Balance deduction on approval is a multi-step write (status change + balance update + audit + notification) and requires a transaction contract.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted (inclusive vs exclusive of end date) and rounded for partial days?
open_questions.impact: Affects used_days deduction on approval and remaining_days computation across all balance call sites; must be consistent everywhere.
candidate_options: Round up to nearest whole day

open_questions.question: How is remaining_days bounded (floor at zero vs allow negative) when used_days exceeds entitlement?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether over-approval is permitted and how balances are displayed/validated.
candidate_options: Reject at approval time if insufficient balance

transaction_contract: The leave approval flow is a multi-step atomic write: update leave_requests.status to APPROVED, deduct used_days from leave_balances, write an audit_logs record, and create a notification. Repository methods that must join a caller's transaction take an optional client/executor parameter (defaulting to the shared pg Pool when omitted). The service owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, issues BEGIN, passes that client to each repository call (LeaveRequestRepository.updateStatus, LeaveBalanceRepository.deduct, AuditLogRepository.create, NotificationRepository.create), then COMMIT on success or ROLLBACK on any failure.
